prediction.overall_explanation: This CometExt contract implements ERC20-like approval functionality with a binary permission system and EIP-712 signature-based authorization. After careful analysis, no exploitable vulnerabilities were found. The allowBySig function properly validates ECDSA signatures with appropriate checks: (1) s-value malleability protection via MAX_VALID_ECDSA_S, (2) v-value validation restricting to 27/28, (3) zero-address check on recovered signatory, (4) owner-signatory match verification, (5) nonce replay protection with increment, and (6) expiry timestamp validation. The nonce check correctly uses post-increment (userNonce[signatory]++) which prevents replay attacks. The domain separator is computed correctly with chainId for cross-chain replay protection. The binary approval system (only accepting uint256.max or 0) is an intentional design choice, not a vulnerability. The contract inherits from CometExtInterface which likely defines storage variables (userNonce, isAllowed, userCollateral, userBasic, etc.) - without seeing this interface, there could be theoretical concerns, but the logic in this contract itself is sound. The name() and symbol() functions safely convert bytes32 to string with proper bounds checking.
